summary: A Rabbi can undo a neder by finding an "opening": a reason the person would not have made it. May he use the honor of the person's father and mother as the opening?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: we may open for a person with the honor of his father and mother.
chunks.explain: We ask: would you have made it if you knew it shames them?
chunks.st: When halakhic authorities are approached with regard to the dissolution of a vow, they may broach dissolution with a person who took a vow by raising the issue of how taking the vow ultimately degraded the honor of his father and mother,
chunks.stMore: asking him the following: Had you known that your parents would experience public shame due to your lax attitude toward your vow, would you still have taken the vow?

chunks.en: But the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer and prohibit

chunks.en: Rabbi Tzadok said,
chunks.st: broaching dissolution of a vow with this particular question. To support the opinion of the Rabbis, Rabbi Tzadok said:

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁפּוֹתְחִין לוֹ בִכְבוֹד אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: "Instead of opening for him with the honor of his father and mother,
chunks.st: Instead of broaching dissolution with him by raising the issue of the honor of his father and mother,

chunks.en: let them open for him with the honor of Hashem.
chunks.st: let them broach dissolution with him by raising the issue of the honor of the Omnipresent.
chunks.stMore: They should point out that a vow taken in the name of God lessens the honor of God, so they could ask him: If you had known that your vow would diminish the honor of God, would you have taken your vow?

chunks.en: If so, there are no nedarim!"
chunks.st: And if so, if this is a valid method of broaching dissolution, there are no vows.

chunks.en: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer about something
chunks.st: Nevertheless, the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer with regard to

chunks.st: a vow concerning a matter that is between him and his father and mother, that

chunks.en: that we may open for him with the honor of his father and mother.
chunks.st: they may broach dissolution with him by raising the issue of the honor of his father and mother, as in this case the extenuation is connected to this particular vow.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer says a Rabbi may undo a neder because of something new that happened later. The Sages say no.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Eliezer also said,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Eliezer further said:

chunks.st: They may broach dissolution by asking about a new situation,

chunks.en: But the Sages forbid it.

chunks.en: How? He said,

chunks.en: and that man became a sofer,
chunks.st: and that person later became a scribe [sofer],

chunks.st: I would not have vowed.

chunks.en: and it became a shul,
chunks.st: and that house became a synagogue,

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, אִלּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא נַעֲשֶׂה
chunks.en: and he said, "If I had known that it would become
chunks.st: and he said: Had I known that it would become

chunks.st: a synagogue, I would not have vowed,

summary: Rabbi Meir says some things only seem new, because they could have happened anyway. The Sages do not agree with him.
stIntro: As a continuation of the opinion of the Rabbis in the previous mishna that they may not broach dissolution of a vow based on a new situation,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵן כְּנוֹלָד וְאֵינָן כְּנוֹלָד,
chunks.en: some things are like something new, but they are not really new,
chunks.st: There are matters that are, at first glance, like a new situation but are not in fact like a new situation,

chunks.en: and the Sages do not agree with him.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis do not concede to him.

chunks.en: How? He said,
chunks.st: How so? For example, one said:

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not marry so-and-so,
chunks.st: Marrying so-and-so is konam

chunks.en: because her father is bad."
chunks.st: for me, as her father is evil,

chunks.en: They told him,
chunks.st: and they told him

chunks.en: "He died," or "He did teshuvah."
chunks.st: that her father died, or that he repented.

chunks.en: "Konam, this house, that I will not go into it,
chunks.st: Or he said: Entering this house is konam for me,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַכֶּלֶב רַע בְּתוֹכוֹ אוֹ שֶׁהַנָּחָשׁ בְּתוֹכוֹ.
chunks.en: because a bad dog is inside, or a snake is inside."
chunks.st: as there is a bad dog inside it, or a snake inside it,

chunks.en: They told him,
chunks.st: and they told him

chunks.en: "The dog died," or "The snake was killed."
chunks.st: that the dog died, or that the snake was killed.

chunks.en: These are like something new, but are not really new,
chunks.st: This is at first glance perceived like a new situation, and yet it is not in fact like a new situation,
chunks.stMore: and this claim may be used to broach dissolution.

chunks.en: and the Sages do not agree with him.
chunks.st: But the Rabbis do not concede to him.

summary: Rabbi Meir says a Rabbi may undo a neder by showing the person that it goes against mitzvos in the Torah, like loving your friend.

chunks.he: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ
chunks.en: And Rabbi Meir also said, we may open for him
chunks.st: And Rabbi Meir further said: The halakhic authorities may broach dissolution with him

chunks.en: from what is written in the Torah, and say to him,
chunks.st: from that which is written in the Torah, and they may say to him:

chunks.en: "If you had known that you are breaking
chunks.st: Had you known that through your vow you are transgressing

chunks.en: 'Do not take revenge' and 'Do not
chunks.st: the prohibition “you shall not take vengeance”

chunks.en: hold a grudge,'
chunks.st: (Leviticus 19:18) and the prohibition “nor bear any grudge”

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא יֵעָנִי וְאֵין אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְפַרְנְסוֹ.
chunks.en: since he may become poor and you cannot help him."
chunks.st: (Leviticus 25:36), as he, the one prohibited by the vow, is poor and now you are not able to provide him with a livelihood due to your vow,
chunks.stMore: would you have vowed in that case?

chunks.he: אָמַר, אִלּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא כֵן,
chunks.en: If he said, "If I had known that it is so,
chunks.st: If he said in reply: Had I known that it is so,

chunks.en: I would not have made the neder,"
chunks.st: that my vow involved all these prohibitions, I would not have vowed;

chunks.en: it is permitted.
chunks.st: it is dissolved.

summary: A Rabbi may undo a neder by reminding the man how much he would have to pay for his wife's kesubah. Rabbi Akiva did this for one man.

chunks.en: We may open for a person with his wife's kesubah.
chunks.st: The halakhic authorities may broach dissolution with a man by raising the issue of his wife’s marriage contract.
chunks.stMore: If one takes a vow that would require him to divorce his wife, e.g., he prohibits her from deriving benefit from him, his vow may be dissolved by asking him whether he had considered how difficult it would be to pay her marriage contract. The mishna relates:

words.note: Kesubah: the money a husband promises his wife.

chunks.en: There was a story with a man who made a neder that his wife may not benefit from him,
chunks.st: And an incident occurred with regard to one who vowed against his wife deriving benefit from him,

chunks.en: and her kesubah was four hundred dinars.
chunks.st: and her marriage contract was worth four hundred dinars.

chunks.en: And he came before Rabbi Akiva,
chunks.st: And he came before Rabbi Akiva,

chunks.en: and he made him give her her kesubah.
chunks.st: and he obligated him to give her the payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: He said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.he: רַבִּי, שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת דִּינָרִין הִנִּיחַ אַבָּא,
chunks.en: "Rebbi, my father left eight hundred dinars,
chunks.st: My teacher, my father left eight hundred dinars

chunks.en: and my brother took four hundred,
chunks.st: as our inheritance, of which my brother took four hundred

chunks.en: and I took four hundred.
chunks.st: and I took four hundred.

chunks.en: Isn't it enough that she takes two hundred,
chunks.st: Isn’t it enough for my wife to take two hundred

chunks.en: and I keep two hundred?"
chunks.st: and I will have two hundred?

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "Even if you sell the hair on your head,
chunks.st: Your claim is not accepted, as even if you sell the hair on your head,

chunks.en: you must give her her kesubah."
chunks.st: you must give her the full payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: He said to him:

chunks.en: "If I had known that it is so,
chunks.st: Had I known that it was so,

chunks.en: I would not have made the neder."
chunks.st: that I would have to give her all my property, I would not have vowed.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Akiva undid it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Akiva permitted her to derive benefit from him.

summary: A Rabbi may undo a neder by asking about Yom Tov and Shabbos. Rabbi Akiva taught that if part of a neder is undone, all of it is undone.

chunks.en: We may open with Yamim Tovim and Shabbosos.
chunks.st: If one vowed that certain food or drink or all food and drink be forbidden to him, the halakhic authorities may broach dissolution by raising the issue of Festivals and Shabbatot.
chunks.stMore: They ask him whether he realized at the time he stated his vow that he would have to uphold it on these festive days as well.

chunks.en: At first they used to say,
chunks.st: At first they said

chunks.en: "Those days are permitted, and the rest
chunks.st: that on those days that he did not intend to include in his vow, that item is permitted, but

chunks.en: of all the days are forbidden,"
chunks.st: on all the rest of the days, food and drink are still forbidden

chunks.en: until Rabbi Akiva came and taught,
chunks.st: by his vow, until Rabbi Akiva came and taught

chunks.en: that a neder that was partly undone
chunks.st: that a vow that is partially dissolved

chunks.en: is all undone.
chunks.st: is dissolved entirely.

summary: More examples of the rule that when part of a neder is undone, all of it is undone, and when it is not.

chunks.en: How? He said,
chunks.st: How so?

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not benefit from all of you,"
chunks.st: In the case of one who said to a group of people: I will not benefit from all of you

chunks.en: if one of them was permitted,
chunks.st: as it is konam for me, if benefit from one of them was permitted

chunks.en: all of them are permitted.
chunks.st: for whatever reason, benefit from all of them is permitted.

chunks.en: "that I will not benefit from this one and this one,"
chunks.st: However, if one said: I will not benefit from this one and from that one

chunks.en: if the first one was permitted,
chunks.st: as it is konam for me, then if benefit from the first one was permitted

chunks.en: all of them are permitted.
chunks.st: for whatever reason, benefit from all of them is permitted.

chunks.en: If the last one was permitted,
chunks.st: But if benefit from the last one was permitted,

chunks.en: the last one is permitted,
chunks.st: benefit from the last one alone is permitted,

chunks.en: and all the others are forbidden.
chunks.st: but benefit from all the others is forbidden,

chunks.en: from him and after is permitted,
chunks.st: then from him and below, i.e., all those enumerated after him, benefit is permitted;

chunks.en: from him and before is forbidden.
chunks.st: from him and above, i.e., those listed before him, benefit is forbidden.

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵינִי נֶהֱנֶה לָזֶה קָרְבָּן וְלָזֶה קָרְבָּן,
chunks.en: "that I will not benefit from this one, a korban, and from this one, a korban,"
chunks.st: The mishna gives another example of interconnected vows: If one stated: I will not benefit from this one, as if he were an offering, and from that one, as if he were an offering,

chunks.en: each and every one needs its own opening.
chunks.st: then an extenuation enabling the dissolution of a vow is required for each and every one, as they have the status of separate vows.

summary: If a person made a neder because he thought something was bad for him, and it turns out some of it is good, the whole neder is undone.

chunks.en: "Konam, wine, that I will not taste,
chunks.st: The mishna gives another example of a vow that was partially dissolved. If one stated in a vow: Wine is konam for me and I will not taste it,

chunks.en: because wine is bad for the stomach."
chunks.st: as wine is bad for the intestines,

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: and they said to him:

chunks.en: "But old wine is good for the stomach!"
chunks.st: But aged wine is good for the intestines,

chunks.en: It is permitted with old wine.
chunks.st: then the vow is dissolved with regard to aged wine.

chunks.en: And not only with old wine is it permitted,
chunks.st: And not only with regard to aged wine is it dissolved,

chunks.en: but with all wine.
chunks.st: but with regard to all types of wine,

chunks.en: "Konam, onion, that I will not taste,
chunks.st: since a vow that has been partially dissolved is entirely dissolved. Likewise, if one stated in a vow: Onions are konam for me and I will not taste them,

chunks.en: because onions are bad for the heart."
chunks.st: as onions are bad for the heart,

chunks.st: But the kuferi onion is good for the heart,

chunks.st: then, in this case too, it is dissolved with regard to kuferi onions,

chunks.st: but with regard to all types of onions.

chunks.st: and Rabbi Meir dissolved the vow with regard to all types of onions.

summary: A Rabbi may undo a neder by asking the man to think about his own good name and his children's good name.

chunks.he: פּוֹתְחִין לָאָדָם בִּכְבוֹד עַצְמוֹ וּבִכְבוֹד בָּנָיו.
chunks.en: We may open for a person with his own honor and the honor of his children.
chunks.st: The halakhic authorities may broach dissolution for a person by raising the issue of his own honor and the honor of his children.

chunks.en: We say to him,
chunks.st: For example, if he took a vow that resulted in his needing to divorce his wife, they may say to him:

chunks.he: אִלּוּ הָיִיתָ יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁלְּמָחָר אוֹמְרִין עָלֶיךָ
chunks.en: "If you had known that tomorrow people will say about you,
chunks.st: Had you known that tomorrow people will say about you:

chunks.en: 'This is the habit of so-and-so,
chunks.st: This is the habit [veset] of so-and-so,

chunks.en: he sends away his wives,'
chunks.st: that he divorces his wives

chunks.en: and about your daughters they will say,
chunks.st: due to vows, and they will say about your daughters:

chunks.en: 'They are daughters of divorced women,
chunks.st: They are daughters of divorce,

chunks.he: מָה רָאֲתָה אִמָּן שֶׁל אֵלּוּ לְהִתְגָּרֵשׁ,
chunks.en: what did their mother do to be divorced?'"
chunks.st: or they will ask: What did their mother see to divorce,

chunks.en: and he said, "If I had known that it is so,
chunks.st: thereby giving them a bad reputation. And if the man who vowed said: Had I known it was so,

chunks.en: I would not have made the neder,"
chunks.st: I would not have vowed,

chunks.en: it is permitted.
chunks.st: it is dissolved.

summary: A neder made because of a mistake does not count. Rabbi Yishmael helped a poor girl look her best, and the neder about her was undone. When he died, the girls of Klal Yisrael cried for him.

chunks.he: קוֹנָם שֶׁאֵינִי נוֹשֵׂא אֶת פְּלוֹנִית כְּעוּרָה,
chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not marry so-and-so, the ugly one,"
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If a man said: Marrying ugly so-and-so is konam for me,

chunks.en: and really she is pretty;
chunks.st: and she is in fact beautiful,

chunks.en: "dark," and really she is fair;
chunks.st: or if, in vowing not to marry her, he called her black, and she is in fact white,

chunks.en: "short," and really she is tall,
chunks.st: or if, in vowing not to marry her, he called her short, and she is in fact tall,

chunks.en: he may marry her.
chunks.st: he is permitted to her.

chunks.he: לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְעוּרָה וְנַעֲשֵׂית נָאָה,
chunks.en: Not because she was ugly and became pretty,
chunks.st: Not because she was ugly and became beautiful,

chunks.en: dark and became fair,
chunks.st: black and became white,

chunks.en: short and became tall,
chunks.st: or short and became tall,

chunks.en: but because the neder was a mistake.
chunks.st: but rather, because the vow was mistaken from the outset.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְאֶחָד שֶׁנָּדַר מִבַּת אֲחוֹתוֹ הֲנָיָה,
chunks.en: There was a story with a man who made a neder not to benefit from his sister's daughter,
chunks.st: The Gemara relates: And an incident occurred with regard to one who vowed against deriving benefit from the daughter of his sister,

chunks.en: and they brought her to Rabbi Yishmael's house and made her look nice.
chunks.st: as he did not wish to marry her. And they brought her into the house of Rabbi Yishmael and he beautified her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael said to him,
chunks.st: When she was later brought before the one who took the vow, Rabbi Yishmael said to him:

chunks.en: "My son, did you make a neder about this one?"
chunks.st: My son, did you vow that you would not derive benefit from this woman?

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: He said to him:

chunks.en: "No." And Rabbi Yishmael undid it.
chunks.st: No, and Rabbi Yishmael permitted her

chunks.he: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בָּכָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְאָמַר,
chunks.en: At that time Rabbi Yishmael cried and said,
chunks.st: to him, as he demonstrated that the vow had been made in error. At that time Rabbi Yishmael wept and said:

chunks.en: "The daughters of Yisrael are pretty,
chunks.st: The daughters of Israel are beautiful,

chunks.en: but being poor makes them look ugly."
chunks.st: but poverty makes them ugly.

chunks.en: And when Rabbi Yishmael died,
chunks.st: And when Rabbi Yishmael died,

chunks.he: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּכֶינָה.
chunks.en: "Daughters of Yisrael, cry for Rabbi Yishmael."
chunks.st: Daughters of Israel, weep for Rabbi Yishmael.

chunks.en: And so it says about Shaul,
chunks.st: And it likewise states about Saul,

chunks.he: א) בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל שָׁאוּל בְּכֶינָה:
chunks.en: "Daughters of Yisrael, cry for Shaul."
